findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: There are cold sandwiches and wraps that are prepared in house and stored in a grab & go cooler near the front entrance. The products lacked proper allergen labeling. Discussed with PIC the need to list allergens on food products so that consumers are aware of potential allergens.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.12 Other Forms of Information. (A) If required by LAW, CONSUMER warnings shall be provided. (B) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or manufacturers' dating information on FOODS may not be concealed or altered. (C) The PERMIT HOLDER shall notify CONSUMERS by written notification of the presence of MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS as an ingredient in unPACKAGED FOOD items that are served or sold to the CONSUMER.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed with debris accumulation:
- Fan guard of the walk in cooler accumulated with dust
- Fan guard above the triple sink where clean dishes are stored (accumulated with dust)

Ensure that fan guards are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the build up of dust and contaminating food and/or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn't a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the time of the inspection. PIC stated that they were in the process of taking the CFM’s course and should be manager certified by the next routine inspection. Ensure that a CFPM is present at all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed the outside door in the back area to be propped open. The door was closed by an employee and a discussion was held with PIC. Ensure that back doors stay shut to prevent entry points for unwanted insects and pests. 

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed several baking utensils and cooking equipment to be stored underneath a fan guard that’s heavily accumulated with dust (on triple sink in bakery area). The utensils and equipment have been cleaned and are in direct contact for possible contamination. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that fan guards are cleaned and maintained as often as necessary to prevent food contact surfaces from being contaminated.  

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed several coolers (in customer areas) to lack hanging thermometers. Ensure all cold holding units have hanging thermometers placed within them. Keep extra thermometers on hand in the back room to replace as needed. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following physical facility repairs in need:
1. The ceiling tiles directly above the oven in the bakery need replaced. Ceiling tiles are burned and brown from oven use. Ceiling tiles should be white in color and smooth and easily cleanable.
2. The 3 compartment sink in the bakery is caulked to the wall properly; however, there is paint missing in areas above the caulking. The wall should be smooth and easily cleanable without drywall exposed.
3. The mop sink needs re-caulked to the wall on several sides of the basin (one side is properly caulked). Caulk is coming away and/or moldy.
4. The mixer next to the reach-in freezers in the bakery has a piece of trim on the wall missing behind the mixer. Repair the wall.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15  (C) Observed the back door to be bent with a gap in the seal upon closing. PIC stated that they have had work done on the door in the past. Ensure the door is sealed so no pests can enter the premesis.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of unidentifiable spices in the bakery kitchen. Unless the contents are easily identifiable, are foods removed from the original package shall be labeled with their contents.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed multiple chest freezers with a heavy accumulation of ice. Defrost chest freezers regularly to allow for a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 1) Observed the large mixing bowls to be left uncovered while the bakery kitchen was shut down. Keep these items covered when not in use to prevent possible contamination of food contact surfaces. 2) Bakery manager is storing his utensils in a wooden chest not intended for holding food contact surfaces. Provide a storage area that is smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable, free of friable material like wood flakes.  750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT 1x> Observed the dry wall in the kitchen below the reach in cooler and mixing bowls to be an unfinished dry wall surface with some gaps. Seal gaps and paint wall to be smooth and easily cleanable. 2) Observed shelf above the mop sink to be a raw wood surface. Paint/seal this area for a smooth, easily cleabable, and non-absorbent surface. 3) Observed areas of the nudo board (top and to the right) above the mop sink to have gaps. Caulk these areas to eliminate gaps.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
REPEAT 1x> 1) Observed a raw wood surfaces above the mop sink. Paint/seal raw wood surfaces to make non-absorbent, smooth, and easily cleanable. REPEAT 1x> 2) Observed the nudo board at the back of the mop sink to not be tightly secured to the wall with a gap present. Secure wall surface and seal all gaps.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the dry wall in the kitchen above the reach in coolers to have an unfinished dry wall surface with some gaps. Paint/seal wall and eliminate gaps.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility could not provide proof of an IL Food Service Sanitation Manager, however, bakery manager (J. Reynolds) stated he passed his FSSMC course and does have his IDPH FSSMC card at home. Inspectors contact information was left with facility. Email or fax FSSMC card information to inspection to avoid a follow up inspector.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
Observed one bowl of mushrooms date marked 10/20. Item was discussed with the bakery manager and he confirmed that the facility was cooking the mushrooms and then cooling as part of food item they provide. Do not cool or reheat any potentially hazardous foods under your medium risk permit. The bowl of mushrooms was discarded to correct the violation.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed multiple chest freezers with an accumulation of ice. Defrost chest freezer to make sure they are smooth and easily cleanable. Ice is not a cleanable surface.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed the sanitizer bucket to have a concentration of 200 ppm chlorine. Provide proper sanitizing concentrations. 100 ppm chlorine of sanitizer buckets (in-place cleaning) and 50 ppm chlorine for manual washing (3 part sink). 2) Observed a wet wiping cloth improperly stored on the counter top. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer buckets between uses. 
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a steady leak at the faucet of the 3 pan sink in the bakery. Repair leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor behind the chest freezers in the back storage area to be soiled with packaging debris and litter. Clean this floor.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT 1x > 1) Observed acoustic ceiling tiles in the employee rest room. Provide smooth and cleanable tiles. REPEAT 1x > 2) Observed the wall outside of the mop sink to be damaged. Repair this wall so its smooth and easily cleanable. 3) Observed 4 holes in the wall above the table top in the bakery. Seal and paint holes to make smooth and easily cleanable. 4)Observed a missing ceiling tile in the bakery. Provide smooth, cleanable ceiling tiles. 5) observed a cut out hole in one of the ceiling tiles above the utensil storage in the bakery. Replace tile.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
